text:
Asha: Quick prototype update — I'm experimenting with a minimal shim that lets us stream legacy safetensors v0 from S3 while preserving our shard-hotspot warmup logic. Wanted quick takes before I turn this into an RFC.
Sam: Nice. How are you thinking about integrity checks for partial downloads?
Luca: I'd push for per-chunk checksums plus a tiny header probe. Extra small HEAD/ranged GETs but we can fail fast on bad ranges.
Asha: Exactly. Plan: synthesize a small sidecar header placed at byte 0 of the object (or served as .meta) that contains a compact chunk index: N entries of (offset, length, checksum). Loader does a small ranged GET for the header (<=16KB), then issues ranged GETs for chunks on-demand. If a ranged GET fails or checksum mismatch -> immediate fallback to mmap/multipart full-download for that shard.
Asha: Rough config I'm testing:
```
loader:
  mode: streaming
  header_probe: 16KB
  chunk_size: 4MB
  header_ttl_s: 60
  fallback_timeout_ms: 120
  fallback_mode: mmap
  hotspot_prefetch_chunks: 2
  checksum_cache: /var/cache/weights-checksums
```
Sam: Tradeoffs: HEAD/probe adds a small hop on cold starts and increases storage metadata a bit. But if hotspot workload benefits from <200ms first-token, it's worth it. Also we should be careful about extra S3 request rates at scale.
Nora: We should instrument: first-byte latency per-shard, ranged GET error rate, checksum_mismatch_count, header_probe_latency, and fallback_triggered_reason (timeout|mismatch|http-error). Dashboards for hot vs non-hot shards.
Luca: Implementation note: keep the shim non-invasive. Do NOT rewrite safetensors to a new format. Offer a sidecar JSON blob with fields: chunk_checksums (base64 list), chunk_byte_offsets (ints), total_size. That keeps other tooling compatible.
Sam: Runtime heuristic: if a shard is tagged in the model manifest as "hotspot", prefetch first K chunks (K=2 default) during warmup; otherwise fetch lazily on first access. That balances memory pressure vs latency.
Asha: Perf guardrails in my prototype: if header_probe_time > fallback_timeout_ms OR first_chunk fetch fails >=2 attempts, mark request to use fallback_mode for that shard and emit metric. We'll tune fallback_timeout_ms after running e2e.
Nora: Add a debug toggle to force fallback so QA/infra can validate both paths without republishing bundles. Also add a safe-mode that only uses mmap for bundles older than X days (migration aid).
infra-bot: CI:nightly - weights-staging e2e scheduled on cluster "weights-staging" at 02:00 UTC (job ws-2026-042). Results will post to #eng-ml after completion.
Asha: Action items: (1) I'll land a small prototype PR with header-synthesis + shim and the loader flags. (2) Nora, can you add the metrics to infra dashboard before the nightly run? (3) Luca, can you draft the exact sidecar JSON schema (two arrays: chunk_checksums, chunk_byte_offsets + total_size + format_version)?
Sam: If we see high ranged GET error rates in nightly, we can try CDN-prefetch for first chunk ranges or add per-region backoff.
Luca: Also consider bundling an optional small manifest file (object.meta.json) next to the shard that contains the sidecar and avoids ranged GET on some storage backends.
Asha: OK — will open the PR and ping reviewers. Keeping the shim tiny should make migration low-risk. :rocket:
